units.text: EXT. RIVER CROSSING - DAY
A swollen brown river, wide and quick.
A stagecoach sits in the middle of it, wheels sunk to the hubs, water slapping at the doors.
The horses stand with heads low, trembling.
DRIVER AMOS PRICKETT (50s, duster, hat tied on with a bandanna) stands on the box with the reins in both fists, staring at the far bank.
Inside, face pressed to the window, sits MRS. LEONORA VASQUEZ-TATE (40s, black traveling dress, hatbox in her lap).
Beside her, a BOY in a derby, ELIJAH "LIJAH" TATE (12, her son), grips the leather strap.
Ma'am, I'd keep still.
units.name: AMOS

units.text: We have been still for an hour.
units.name: LEONORA

units.text: Then you're good at it.
units.name: AMOS

units.text: The coach shifts.
The hatbox slides.
Lijah catches it.
Ma, the water's coming in.
units.name: LIJAH

units.text: I see it.
units.name: LEONORA

units.text: Is it going to tip?
units.name: LIJAH

units.text: She doesn't answer.
Her gloved hand reaches over and settles over his, over the strap, over the hatbox.
Whole thing's gonna shift. When it does, you climb up here, both of you. Don't look down.
units.name: AMOS

units.text: Leonora and Lijah both reach for the door.
Amos swears, swings down onto the roof, and hooks an arm through the luggage rail; the coach lurches, the horses scream, and Leonora tumbles into her son.
They tangle in the narrow seat for a second, then Amos throws open the door and hauls them up one after the other onto the box.
They crouch there, three figures in a row on the top of a sinking coach.
The water tugs at the wheels.
Somewhere on the far bank, a dog begins to bark.
Mister Prickett?
units.name: LIJAH

units.text: Yeah.
units.name: AMOS

units.text: I lost my hat.
units.name: LIJAH

units.text: Amos looks.
The derby is floating away on the current, turning like a leaf.
Reckon it's going where we're going.
units.name: AMOS

units.text: Amos.
units.name: LEONORA

units.text: Ma'am.
units.name: AMOS

units.text: She opens the hatbox.
Inside, folded in tissue, lies a child's christening gown.
She lifts it out.
She holds it to her face.
I don't want it to be ruined.
units.name: LEONORA

units.text: It won't be.
units.name: AMOS

units.text: She gives it to Lijah.
He tucks it inside his shirt.
The coach settles, and holds.
The horses start forward on their own.
The wheels bite the river bed.
Slowly, with a groan of timber, they climb toward the bank.
